findings.summary: the rendered PNG carries no text: no title, no arm names, no share/interval labels and no axis tick labels. Pixel analysis of the attached image is unambiguous — the title band (y < 45) and the arm label column (x < 300) contain zero non-white pixels, and the only dark marks are the interval whiskers — so the six bars are unattributable and their values unreadable. This is the reader-facing artifact the review judges, and it does not let a reader read the figure.

the SVG root declares only font-family="system-ui, sans-serif" and font-size="13"; the rasterizer that produced the attached PNG resolved no glyphs for it (while this host's fontconfig falls the list back to DejaVu Sans). The script does emit every missing label (title at :1278, arm names at :1292, share/interval at :1309, tick labels at :1318), so the anomaly is a text-rendering dependency: the figure's legibility depends on the renderer's font discovery rather than on the document. Naming an installed family, or re-rendering with a font-capable rasterizer, would settle whether the artifact or the export path is at fault.

colour is the only marker separating the control arms (orange #e07a5f: incumbent and withheld/one-pass/frontier) from the model arms (blue #4b7bec), and nothing identifies that mapping: the script draws no legend, the evidence fragment says nothing about colour, and the figure has no caption. Even once text renders, a reader cannot learn what the orange bars are from the figure.

vertical gridlines are the only decoration in the plot area; the house plot style leaves gridlines out and despines the axes, and the tick labels they every 20 % sit under are themselves missing from the rendered PNG. Removing them costs no data.

the figure is written to docs/figures/sn-case-file-generation/scfg-benchmark/heldout-arm-right.svg but referenced nowhere: `git grep heldout-arm-right c752333edbef -- docs/` finds only this line, so no evidence fragment or plan page embeds it and a reader of the evidence page never sees the artifact.
